 2026 General Election: A Northwest Montana Voter’s Guide to Local, State and Federal Races 
 Absentee ballots went out Oct. 9, and Election Day is Nov. 3. Flathead Valley voters will weigh an open U.S. Senate seat, an open western congressional seat, a state Supreme Court contest, three ballot measures and a full slate of legislative and county races. Here’s what to know.
 By Beacon Staff 
 November 3, 2026 
 -->
 Voting booths at the Election Department at the Flathead County North Complex in Kalispell on Nov. 3, 2026. Hunter D’Antuono | Flathead Beacon 
 Editor’s Note: This voter’s guide will be updated between now and Election Day, Nov. 3, as we publish additional stories and candidate responses. Check back for the latest. 
 Last updated: Nov. 2 at 1 p.m. 
 Montana’s general election lands on Nov. 3 this fall, following a campaign cycle characterized by last-minute switch-ups, mysterious PACs and tight races. For those who want to make their voices heard in this year’s election, ballots are due by 8 p.m. Tuesday.
 Absentee ballots were first mailed out Oct. 9, and at this point, should be hand-delivered to your designated polling place or to the Flathead County Elections Office, located at 290 B N. Main St. in Kalispell. For a full list of polling locations, visit votemt.gov .
 That website, run by the secretary of state, also allows voters who have already returned absentee ballots to check and ensure their ballots were received.
 For those who didn’t receive an absentee ballot and plan to vote in person this week, polling places are statutorily required to be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day. And while a 2025 state law aimed to limit Election Day voter registration, it was blocked from going into place, which means voters can still show up and register to vote until 8 p.m. on Election Day. As long as voters are in line by 8 p.m. Tuesday, they should be allowed to cast a ballot. Voters can also register through noon on Monday.
 To vote in person or register to vote on Election Day, voters must bring a photo ID with them. Acceptable forms of identification include a valid driver’s license or REAL ID, a Montana state identification card, a military ID, a tribal photo ID, a U.S. passport, a concealed-carry permit or a Montana University System photo ID. For those who don’t have one of the listed options, they must present a photo ID alongside a utility bill, bank statement, paycheck or other government document that shows a name and address.
 On their ballots, Flathead Valley voters will select their preferred candidates in the U.S. Senate race and for Montana’s western congressional district. In the Senate race, Republican Kurt Alme, Democrat Alani Bankhead, independent Seth Bodnar and Libertarian Kyle Austin are vying for the seat. In the western congressional district, Republican Aaron Flint, Democrat Sam Forstag and Libertarian Nick Sheedy are competing to succeed U.S. Rep. Ryan Zinke.
 Voters will also choose between Flathead district judges Amy Eddy and Dan Wilson for a seat on the Montana Supreme Court, decide the Public Service Commission’s District 5 race, and fill four state Senate and 13 state House seats in the Flathead and surrounding counties, along with a Flathead County commission seat. They’ll also vote on three statewide ballot measures: Initiative 194, and Constitutional Initiatives 132 and 133.
 – Beacon Staff
